subject: Uplift / annualize offset agreement and procurement timing
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uplift / annualize offset agreement and procurement timing

Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick note to capture the path we discussed and propose two concrete options so procurement has something to review next week.

Summary of Brightline ask: mid-contract capacity increase (~35% uplift) with a co-term to your existing renewal date and an ask to apply a partial annualization (offset) so you don’t pay full unit price for the shortened period. You also requested flexibility on invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and a limited holdback for forecasting risk.

Option A — Staged annualize (preferred)
- 35% uplift allocated to a separate top-up bucket for the remainder of current term.
- Convert 50% of the uplift to an annualized invoice at a blended rate prorated for term length; remaining 50% billed as true-up at next renewal at a reduced uplift rate.
- 10% goodwill credit applied to the true-up if Brightline hits the forecasted usage threshold.
- No change to SLA; standard Dedicated SLAs preserved.

Option B — Immediate pro-rate + voucher
- Full uplift invoiced pro-rata for remaining months at list uplift rate, plus a future voucher equivalent to 15% of uplift value redeemable within 12 months.
- Allows immediate capacity, but higher near-term cash outlay.

Attachments: I attached an XLSX with line-item math (Redwood_uplift_options_Q3.xlsx) and a short draft amendment to show the expected legal footprint.

Next steps: If procurement prefers Option A we can draft an amendment and route for signature (DocuSign link included once countersigned). If preferences differ, happy to hop on a 20-min call with Tim/Contracts to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Michael

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@brightlinehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uplift / annualize offset agreement and procurement timing

Thanks Michael — appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying points from procurement and finance after an internal review: 

1) Cashflow sensitivity: finance would prefer Option A if the blended near-term invoice can be capped so it doesn't exceed 60% of the expected monthly run-rate; otherwise they will push for Option B (voucher) because it limits immediate spend.
2) Forecast trigger: we like the idea of the 10% goodwill credit tied to usage but need a firm definition of the trigger (e.g., average monthly usage >= 95% of uplifted units across two consecutive months).
3) PO & invoicing: Contracts need invoices to align with a PO amendment; does Redwood support signed amendment + net-30 on amended line items?
4) Legal redlines: we will push a short set of standard redlines on indemnity and data retention for the amendment (low-risk).

Can you ask legal to keep the amendment scoped to only: term, uplift units, invoicing cadence, and the voucher/credit language? We want to avoid re-opening other clauses.

Happy to have Tim (cc'd) or our contracts inbox continue coordination. If you can provide a tightened Option A that ensures the near-term cap + a precise credit trigger, we can move quickly.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Procurement
Brightline Health

Looping you both in — procurement at Brightline wants a tightened version of Option A with a near-term invoice cap and a firm usage trigger for the credit. Key asks below; can one of you run numbers and produce a one-pager and a redline-ready amendment?

Key constraints from Brightline:
- Near-term invoice cap: <= 60% of expected monthly run-rate for the remaining term (finance)
- Credit trigger: prefer 2-month consecutive average >= 95% of uplifted units
- Legal scope: only term, uplift, invoicing cadence, voucher/credit — no other contractual changes

Ben — can you provide a blended rate that meets the cap constraint (showing math for 50/50 annualize vs true-up) and list the impact on Redwood revenue recognition? Neha — can you have legal produce a 1-page amendment redline that restricts scope as requested? I drafted updated numbers in the attached sheet (see tab 'CapScenario').

I propose: internal target to send tightened Option A + amendment to Brightline by EOD Thursday (2026-04-09). If we need to push procurement to sign earlier, offer a one-time 5% implementation credit applied at next renewal rather than additional near-term discount.

Thanks — Michael

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and timing. We ran the numbers and attached a concise offer and the redline amendment (attached PDF) scoped to the four items you requested. Highlights: 

- Offer (tightened Option A): 35% uplift; 50% annualize / 50% true-up. Blended near-term invoice will be capped at 58% of projected monthly run-rate (meets your <=60% requirement). Detailed math in the XLSX "CapScenario" tab.
- Credit trigger: defined as average monthly usage across the uplift bucket >= 95% for any two consecutive months within the remainder of the term; credit = 10% of uplift invoiced value applied as a credit against the true-up at renewal.
- Invoicing & PO: Redwood will accept an amendment + PO; amended line items will be Net-30 from invoice date.
- Legal: we kept redlines tightly scoped; no other clauses opened.

If that aligns, we can initiate DocuSign (link below) and route to finance/legal. If Brightline needs a 1-week review period, we can hold the offer for 7 calendar days.
